prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Ay, gaze upon her rose-wreathed hair, And gaze upon her smile; Seem as you drank the very air Her breath perfumed the while: And wake for her the gifted line, That wild and witching lay, And swear your heart is as a shrine, That only owns her sway. ’Tis well: I am revenged at last,— Mark you that scornful cheek,— The eye averted as you pass’d, Spoke more than words could speak. Ay, now by all the bitter tears That I have shed for thee,— The racking doubts, the burning fears,— Avenged they well may be— By the nights pass’d in sleepless care, The days of endless woe; All that you taught my heart to bear, All that yourself will know. I would not wish to see you laid Within an early tomb; I should forget how you betray’d, And only weep your doom: But this is fitting punishment, To live and love in vain,— Oh my wrung heart, be thou content, And feed upon his pain. Go thou and watch her lightest sigh,— Thine own it will not be; And bask beneath her sunny eye,— It will not turn on thee. ’Tis well: the rack, the chain, the wheel, Far better hadst thou proved; Ev’n I could almost pity feel, For thou art not beloved.

outputs.L2:
Here is a rewrite of the text using completely different phrasing and sentence structures while retaining every detail of the original:

Go ahead and admire her floral-decorated hair and her smile. Act as if the very atmosphere you breathe is made sweet by her presence. Write brilliant, mesmerizing poetry in her honor, and pledge that your heart worships only her command. 

This pleases me, for my revenge has finally arrived. Look at her disdainful expression—the way she averted her gaze when you walked past said more than any spoken words ever could. 

Indeed, all the bitter tears I cried over you, along with the agonizing uncertainty and burning anxiety I felt, are now fully repaid. The endless days of sorrow and the sleepless nights filled with worry that you forced me to endure are the exact same tortures you will now experience yourself. 

I do not wish for your life to end prematurely in the grave, because if that happened, I might forget your betrayal and merely mourn your death. Instead, continuing to live while loving someone in vain is the rightful penalty. My suffering heart can now be at peace and draw satisfaction from your pain. 

Go ahead and pay attention to her faintest sigh, knowing it is not meant for you, and try to take comfort in her bright eyes, knowing she will never look your way. Truly, enduring physical torture on the rack, wheel, or chains would have been much easier for you to bear. Because you are not loved in return, even I feel a moment of near-compassion for you.
outputs.L3:
There is a dark, poetic irony in watching you fall to your knees. For all your past pride, you have finally surrendered your heart to a woman who views it as nothing more than a trivial souvenir. You burn for her, yet she offers you only ice—meeting your desperate devotion with cold scorn and utter indifference. 

For years, I carried the unbearable weight of the agony you so carelessly inflicted upon me. I bled silently from the wounds of your deceit, wondering if the universe would ever hold you accountable for the heart you shattered without a second thought. Now, I see that justice was merely taking its time. Your current undoing is not a tragic twist of fate; it is the long-awaited answer to my pain, a sweet and silent retribution crafted specifically for you.

If you believe I wish for your death, you misunderstand the depth of my grievance. A swift end would be a mercy—an easy escape from the consequences of your cruelty. Death brings peace, and peace is the last thing you deserve. No, living is your true sentence. Your punishment is to wake up every morning trapped in the purgatory of your own yearning, forced to carry the crushing weight of an unrequited soul.

I find a profound, almost intoxicating satisfaction in this complete reversal of roles. To watch you wither under the exact same agony you once forced me to endure—to know that you now bleed for someone who will never care if you live or die—is a far greater recompense than any apology you could ever offer. At long last, the scales are balanced, and your hell is to feel every drop of the misery you so recklessly gave away.
outputs.L4:
For months, the ghost of your betrayal was a physical weight in my chest—a sharp, persistent ache that refused to settle into a scar. I had given you a devotion that was absolute, only to be cast aside like a temporary distraction when your eyes caught the light of someone new. In the quiet aftermath of your departure, I confess I prayed for your ruin. I wished for your world to crumble with the same sudden, violent finality that yours had brought to mine.

Yet, fate proved far more creative than my bitterest thoughts. 

I watched from the shadows as you threw yourself into the orbit of a woman made of marble and frost. The pride that once defined you evaporated, replaced by an embarrassing, frantic desperation. You, who had handled my heart so carelessly, were suddenly on your knees, offering up every piece of your soul to someone who treated your existence as a minor inconvenience. You wrote letters she left unopened; you made grand gestures that met only her polite, devastating boredom. 

Her cruelty lay not in malice, but in utter indifference. She did not hate you—she simply did not care. 

Seeing you shattered by her casual disdain should have brought me a shameful, fleeting pleasure. Instead, it brought something much deeper: a quiet, absolute vindication. In those early, dark days of my grief, I believed that death—or some sudden tragedy—was the only fitting punishment for the damage you had caused. I thought your silence in the grave would balance the scales. 

I was wrong. Death is a mercy. It is a swift, silent end to suffering, a light extinguished all at once. It grants the relief of nonexistence. 

Your true sentence is the life you are now condemned to lead. To wake each morning with a heart full of agonizing hope, to spend your days striving for a smile that will never be meant for you, and to fall asleep beneath the crushing weight of your own irrelevance—that is a far more exquisite retribution. You are trapped in a purgatory of your own making, bound to love a phantom who will never love you back. 

My pain has finally receded, leaving behind a clear, cool peace. I no longer wish you ill, nor do I wish you dead. It is enough to leave you exactly where you are: alive, entirely conscious, and doomed to love in vain.

She stood at the edge of the quiet garden, watching the twilight drift slowly across the hills. To a casual observer, **her** thoughts might **seem** distant, lost somewhere in the fading warmth of the late afternoon sun. **And** yet, beneath that tranquil exterior lay a mind that was entirely present, taking in the rustle of the leaves, the cool breath of the evening wind, and the steady rhythm of the world settling into night.

Distance has a subtle way of altering perception. Things are rarely as simple as they first **seem**, **and** those who spent time in **her** company quickly learned to look beyond the surface. **Her** quiet nature was not an absence of feeling, but a deliberate stillness—a space where thoughts could mature before being spoken. **And** in that quiet strength, she moved through the world with a calm grace that left a lasting impression on everyone she met.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a Victorian-style poem about feeling revenged when an ex-lover suffers unrequited love from someone else.
counterfactuals.output:
Thou cast my devotion to wither away,
And turned thy cold face from my weeping that day;
Thou mocked at the sorrow that burdened my breast,
And left my poor heart in its ruin to rest.
Thou deemedst me frail for the tears that I shed,
And walked from our love with a pitiless tread.

Yet Fate, with her mirror of shadow and steel,
Hath turned the dark spoke of her glittering wheel;
Thou bowest thy knee to a lady so fair,
Who answers thy suit with an icy despair.
Thou offerest pearls, and the soul in thy chest,
To one who regards thee a phantom at best.

She looks through thy pleading with unseeing eyes,
And heeds not the tempest of desperate sighs;
She scorns all the blossoms thou lay’st at her feet,
And leaves thee to wander the desolate street.
Thou waitest in vain by her iron-wrought gate,
To beg for a glance from the queen of thy fate.

How sweet is the poison thou’rt driven to taste!
The very same sorrow, the very same waste!
The chalice of wormwood thou proffered to me
Is pressed by Nemesis in silence to thee.
Thou knowest at last what it is to be spurned—
The ashes of grief to the altar returned.

I watch from the shadows, unheeded, serene,
And drink the rich wine of this desolate scene.
No longer I mourn for the vows thou hast slain,
For thy agony balances all of my pain.
Unrequited thou bleedest, unpitied thou art—
A sovereign revenged in the depths of my heart.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a dramatic poem from the perspective of someone who was betrayed by their lover. The speaker watches as the former lover falls hopelessly in love with a new woman who completely rejects him, finding satisfaction in knowing he is finally experiencing the exact heartbreak he inflicted.
counterfactuals.output:
You left me a phantom in the rooms we built,
A quiet ghost clutching a severed thread.
I drowned in the ocean of your unearned guilt,
While you walked away to a warmer bed.
You broke me with ease, like a dry winter reed,
And laughed as I bled on the marble floor.
I begged for a crumb of the love that I’d need,
While you slammed down the heavy, iron door.

But look at you now, in the shadows cast,
A beggar where once you wore a crown.
You have met your sweet altar of ruin at last,
And she drags your proud spirit down.

I watch from the dark as you drop to your knees,
Offer your soul like a desperate prayer.
You tremble and whisper, you stammer and plead,
Entangled inside her indifferent stare.
She is beautiful, yes—a wild, cruel sun—
And you are the moth she burns to ash.
You give her the worship you gave to no one,
And she breaks your heart with a careless lash.

She turns on her heel. She doesn't even look back.
She leaves you stranded in the freezing rain.
And there you collapse on the very same track
Where you left me to wither in desperate pain.

How does it taste, my darling, my thief?
The dust in your mouth? The iron in your chest?
Do you recognize the shape of this suffocating grief?
It’s the very same poison you offered your guest.

Do you hear my old tears in the sound of your sob?
Does the silence scream back with the words that I spoke?
You stole every piece that a lover could rob,
And now you are choking on the fire you broke.

I feel no grand pity. I lend you no grace.
I offer no hand to pull you from the deep.
I simply stand back, a cold smile on my face,
And harvest the agony you sowed for me to keep. 

Drink it all down. Let it burn, let it sting.
Suffer the winter you crafted so well.
It is sweet poetic justice to watch a tyrant king
Beg for a drop of water in his own homemade hell.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a 19th-century Romantic poem exploring the bitter satisfaction of seeing an unfaithful partner get rejected, using archaic language and vivid emotional imagery.
counterfactuals.output:
Thou sworest love as boundless as the sea,
Then cast my bleeding spirit to the shade;
Thou fled’st my side in fickle vanity,
To tender vows where new desire strayed.

How proudly didst thou weave thy web of art,
To win the maid thy restless eyes pursued!
Thou deemed’st to ensnare another heart
With the same guile that my poor youth subdued.

Yet lo! She sensed the serpent in thy breast,
And read the falsehood written on thy brow;
With freezing scorn she spurned thy warm request,
And left thee shuddering in the shadows now.

I mark thy ruin through the midnight chill,
I see thee grovel where thou thought’st to reign;
No pity stirs my silent bosom still—
I drink the nectar of thy present pain.

A bitter comfort blooms from thy despair,
As Fate repays the anguish born of old;
Thy kneeling shadow pleads to empty air,
Thy fiery passion turned to sudden cold.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem about the ultimate revenge: watching the person who broke your heart love someone who will never love them back.
counterfactuals.output:
I never crafted a malicious plot,
Nor wished for lightning from a sudden sky;
I only kept the bruises that you gave,
And watched the quiet years go drifting by.

For vengeance is a blade that cuts the hand,
And anger is a fire that burns the home.
I simply sat outside the tragedy,
And let the slow, unyielding karma roam.

And oh, the play is beautiful to watch:
You’ve built an altar for a ghost of glass.
You pour your sacred water on the stone,
And beg the freezing winter not to pass.

You send the messages they never read;
You analyze their silence for a sign.
You reach to touch a hand that pulls away,
The exact way that I used to reach for thine.

They look at you with calm, indifferent eyes,
Immune to all the worship that you bring.
To them, you are a shadow in the hall,
A brief distraction, not a sacred thing.

Now you have learned the agony of hope,
The slow starvation of an open heart—
To bleed for one who doesn't feel your pain,
And watch your desperate world be torn apart.

I lift my glass and watch you from the dark,
No poison in the cup, no blood to spill.
The sweetest sentence ever passed by fate:
To watch you love a heart you cannot fill.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a poem in the style of Letitia Elizabeth Landon or Lord Byron about unrequited love, betrayal, and poetic justice.
counterfactuals.output:
**The False Shrine: A Nemesis**

I offered thee a heart untaught to feign,
  A love as boundless as the midnight sea;
Thou took’st the offering, but returned it—pain,
  And smiled to break the soul that lived for thee.
Thou turnedst away to worship lighter shrines,
  Where gilded flattery masked the secret sneer;
Thou couldst not read the agony in lines
  Traced by a hand that held thy memory dear.

I did not weep; the proud mask not their tears
  To feed the triumphs of a heart of stone.
I locked my anguish in the vault of years,
  And learned the bitter lesson: stand alone.
Thou deemedst me defeated, crushed, outworn,
  A faded shadow in thy sunlit track,
While thou didst revel in thy youthful scorn,
  Nor dreamed the dark Avenger glances back.

Yet Time, the ruthless arbener of pride,
  Moves on slow wings to strip thy summer bloom;
The fickle crowd that fluttered at thy side
  Fles at the first cold herald of thy doom.
The false smiles vanish, and the courtly praise
  Dies like an echo on a desolate plain,
And in the silence of thy ruined days,
  Thou sit’st alone with shadow and disdain.

Now in the hush of thine unheeded night,
  When hollow vanity no longer warms,
Thou’lt look in vain for that devotion’s light,
  And stretch thy cold hands to the empty storms.
Thou’lt crave the love thou once didst cast away,
  And plead to lips that will no more reply;
Thy late remorse shall make the shadows gray,
  Unwept, untreasured, and unmourned to die.

Thou’lt learn at last how sharp the weapon turns,
  When hopeless passion chills the bleeding breast;
My heart no longer for thy presence burns—
  Thou hast thy poetic doom: *to love, and be unblest.*
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
